L54: ## Call for Papers
L55: 
L56: 202 7 IEEE Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA 202 7) will take place in Seoul,
L57: Republic of Korea on May 24-28, 202 7.
L58: 
L59: Being the flagship conference of the IEEE Robotics and Automation Society, ICRA will bring together the world’s top researchers and leading companies to share ideas and advances in Robotics and Automation. The conference will include plenary sessions, contributed paper sessions, workshops and tutorial sessions, forums, exhibitions, and robot competitions.
L60: Important Dates:
L61:   * ~~Paper submission deadline: September 16, 2026 (23:59 PST)~~ (via cite30†Paperplaza†ras.papercept.net )
L62: ~~ * Submission Deadline Extended~~
L63:   * ~~Submission of accompanying videos: ~~ ~~Open (1) Aug 5-Sep 9, 2026, ~~ ~~and (2) Sep 18-22, 2026 (23:59 PST)~~.
L64:   * Notification of acceptance/rejection: January 31, 2027 (Sun)
L65:   * Paperplaza opens for final submission: February 6, 202 7 (Fri)
L66:   * Author registration deadline:  March 5, 2027 (Fri)
L67:   * Early Registration deadline:  March 31, 2027 (Wed)
L68:   * Deadline Standard Registration deadline: May 14, 2027 (Fri)
L69: Please note:
L70: 
L71: ICRA 202 7 will be an on-site conference. There will be no option to present a paper online.
L72: If there is no on-site presenter, the paper will be considered as no-show and skipped.
L73: 
L74: If your paper is found to be in violation of IEEE-RAS AI use policies and is subsequently disqualified or withdrawn from the conference program, your registration fees will NOT be refunded.
L75: ### Preparing your Submission
L76: The page limit is 8 pages for the complete paper (text, figures, tables, acknowledgement, bibliography/references). Papers exceeding the 8 page limit at the time of submission will be returned without review. All papers must be submitted in PDF and must follow the ICRA double column format. ICRA applies the double anonymous review process as defined by RAS: cite31†Rules for the Double-Anonymous Review Process – IEEE Robotics and Automation Society Website†nam12.safelinks.protection.outlook.com .
L77: Information and templates are available cite32†here†nam12.safelinks.protection.outlook.com .
L78: ### SUBMISSION OF ACCOMPANYING VIDEOS
L79: 
L80: We strongly encourage authors to submit a video clip to complement the paper submission. Please note that a video that was NOT submitted with the initial submission of an ICRA paper (during the two submission windows), will NOT be accepted at a later date.
L81: 
L82: Video uploads will be unavailable between 10 September and 16 September 2026, to allow the unhindered uploading/updating of the PDF manuscripts of contributed papers during that period.
L83: Detailed Video submission guidelines for contributed ICRA papers:
L84: 
L85:   * File size: up to 20MB
L86:   * Format (only one of the following should be used): mpeg, mp4, mpg
L87:   * Maximum duration: 180 sec.
L88:   * Minimum height: 480
L89:   * Minimum frame rate (fps): 20
L90:   * Scan type: Progressive
L91: ### RESUBMISSION OF PAPERS REJECTED FROM IROS 2026​
L92: 
L93: ICRA 2027 offers a submission category “IROS-ICRA transfer” for papers that previously were submitted to IROS 2026 but were not accepted for publication. The submission should include an additional Author Response File (PDF) to clarify how the comments from the AE/Editor and the reviewers were taken into account in the preparation of the revised paper. The papers will undergo a regular review process.​
L94: It is authors’ responsibility to not identify themselves in the response file.​
L95: 
L96: It is also the authors’ responsibility to download reviewers’ comments for the rejected paper and make it a part of author responses.
L97: ### PRESENTATION OF ACCEPTED RAS JOURNAL PAPERS
L98: Authors of accepted papers from the RAS sponsored conferences RAM, RA-L, T-ASE, T-RO, T-RL, T-FR, RA-P, and ToH are automatically offered the option to present their paper at a RAS conference upon notification of final acceptance. Paperplaza supports direct transfer of papers from T-RO, RA-M, RA-L, and T-RL to ICRA 2027. For transfer of papers from other journals the paper must be manually uploaded to ICRA under the submission category “external journal submission”.
L99: For this a submission code is required, which can be obtained from the journal. Please, check the webpage of the journals for further information and eligibility time windows: cite33†RAS sponsored publications†www.ieee-ras.org . The deadline for transfer of journal papers to ICRA 2027 is 31 st December 2026.
L100: ### For Authors: Guidelines regarding the use and disclosure of AI tools​
L101: 
L102: ​If your paper is found to be in violation of IEEE-RAS AI use policies and is subsequently disqualified or withdrawn from the conference program, your registration fees will NOT be refunded.
L103: Generative AI tools and technologies, such as ChatGPT, may not be listed as authors of a paper submitted to ICRA 202 7. The use of content generated by AI in an article (including but not limited to text, figures, images, and code) must be disclosed in the acknowledgments section.
L104: The AI system used must be identified, and specific sections of the article that use AI-generated content should be specified and accompanied by a brief explanation regarding the manner in which the AI system was used to generate the content. The use of AI systems for editing and grammar enhancement is common practice and, as such, is generally outside the intent of the above policy.
L105: Information or content contained in or about a manuscript under review shall not be processed through an AI system. Doing so is considered a breach of confidentiality and as such is not permitted.
L106: ### Note for authors who require a CC BY open access license
L107: 
L108: Please note that some authors (such as those funded by UKRI) require a “Creative Commons Attribution Only License – Open Access” (CC BY) license for their papers. If you require a CC BY license for your paper, please follow the guidelines described under option 2 on the following website: cite34†https://open.ieee.org/ieee-compliance-with-ukri/†open.ieee.org L109: ### FAQ
L110: 
L111: What is this year’s motto? Which topic areas are covered by the conference?​
L112: 
L113: Traditionally, ICRA covers all areas of robotics research. In order to find out if your paper will fit to the conference, you may want to check the ICRA keywords. You can find the complete list of ICRA keywords here: cite35†Keywords – IEEE Robotics and Automation Society (ieee-ras.org)†urldefense.com ​
L114: 
L115: When you submit a paper, you should select at least three keywords from this list.
L116: Is the ICRA review process single-blind or double-blind?​
L117: 
L118: The ICRA review process is double-anonymous (both reviewers and authors stay anonymous). Therefore, manuscripts should exclude the authors and their affiliations. However, when all the co-authors must be entered in Paperplaza at the time of first submission. The author information will be visible to the editors and AEs only, but not to reviewers.​
L119: You can find templates here: cite36†Important Information for Manuscript Preparation (papercept.net)†urldefense.com L120: 
L121: Can I add supplementary material in the paper or as an attachment?​
L122: 
L123: The allowed paper length is 8 pages, meaning 8 pages for the complete paper content, including all material, acknowledgments, and references. Any supplementary material must fit within the 8 regular pages. A video attachment is possible.
L124: 
L125: Will there be an extension to the paper submission deadline?​
L126: There is no plan to extend the paper submission deadline.​
L127: 
L128: Can I add weblinks in the paper?​
L129: 
L130: You can include URLs (not links embedded in the pdf), but you should not expect that reviewers will look at those links, or that they will influence the review process. Beyond the submitted paper and the (optional) supplementary video, reviewers are not required to look at any other material when writing their reviews.​
L131: Please find more information of the PDF requirements on  cite37†Compliance (papercept.net)†urldefense.com .​
L132: 
L133: Is it allowed to submit a paper that previously was published at a workshop or on a preprint server (e.g. arxiv)?
L134: IEEE supports the evolutionary publication paradigm of workshop papers being improved to conference papers, which are then improved to journal papers. Therefore, papers, which previously have been published at a workshop without formal/peer reviewed proceedings, can be submitted to ICRA. Similarly, papers, which have been uploaded on a preprint server (e.g. arxiv) and are not submitted simultaneously to any other conference or journal, can be submitted to ICRA.​
L135: However, if your workshop paper has a DOI, this would be considered as an archival publication equivalent to a conference paper. Such papers cannot be submitted.
L136: 
L137: How can I transfer an accepted paper from T-ASE/T-FR/RA-P /ToH for presentation at ICRA?
L138: If you want to transfer an accepted paper from one of the journals T-ASE, T-FR, RA-P, or ToH to ICRA, the paper should be submitted in paperplaza in the submission category “External journal submission” of ICRA. Do not submit it as a regular ICRA paper! For the paper upload, you will need to enter a code, which can be obtained from the Editor-In-Chief of the journal.​
L139: Notice that papers from T-RO, RA-M,RA-L, and T-RL follow a different process and do not require a code. Authors of accepted papers will receive an email from PaperCept regarding the transfer of their paper to a conference at which they wish to present their paper.​
L140: 
L141: The deadline for all transfers of journal papers to ICRA 2027 is 31 December 2026.​
L142: ### Organizer and Speaker Registration
L143: 
L144: All conference organizers and speakers attending in person must register to access workshops and tutorials.
L145: 
L146: ICRA 2025 offers a workshop/tutorial-only registration option, allowing organizers and speakers to register exclusively for the sessions they are participating in, instead of registering for the full conference. Please refer to the ICRA cite15†registration page for this purpose.
L147: ### Student Registration
L148: 
L149: All onsite student attendees (for workshops/tutorials) must register either for the workshops or for the entire conference to gain access.
L150: 
L151: Student members are eligible for discounted registration fees, as detailed on the cite15†ICRA 2025 website .
L152: ### Coffee and Lunch Breaks
L153: 
L154:   * Morning break: 10:00 AM – 11:00 AM
L155:   * Afternoon break: 3:00 PM – 4:00 PM
L156: 
L157: Workshop/tutorial organizers are recommended to schedule their breaks within these time slots.
L158: 
L159: Please note: ICRA 2025 does not provide lunch during workshop days. The designated lunch break is from 12:30 PM to 1:30 PM.
L160: ### Workshop and Tutorial Timing
L161: 
L162:   * Full-day workshops: 8:30 AM – 5:30 PM
L163:   * Half-day tutorials:
L164:     * Morning session: 8:30 AM – 12:30 PM
L165:     * Afternoon session: 1:30 PM – 5:30 PM
L166: ### Remote Attendance
L167: 
L168: Presenters and attendees who are unable to attend in person may participate remotely.
L169: 
L170: Workshop organizers must create and provide the necessary streaming links for their sessions. Please note:
L171: 
L172:   * Conference internet may be unreliable, though fewer connectivity issues are expected during workshop days due to lower usage.
L173:   * If you plan to stream your workshop, you are responsible for handling the setup.
L174: ### Additional Information
L175: 
L176:   * There is no minimum number of registrants required for a workshop to proceed. Workshops will NOT be canceled due to low registration.
L177:   * We will soon provide workshop organizers with details on:
L178:     * Standard room setups and AV equipment
L179:     * A request form for special requirements
L180:     * An estimated number of posters needed

L90:     * cite26†AI Policy for Authors L91:   * cite0†Organization L92:     * cite27†Board L93: # ICLR 2027 Author Guidelines
L94: Similar to previous years, for ICLR 2027 we are asking authors to submit paper abstracts by the earlier abstract submission deadline of Sep 18, 2026 AOE The full paper submission deadline is Sep 25, 2026 AOE. Abstracts and papers must be submitted using the conference submission system at: cite28†https://openreview.net/group?id=ICLR.cc/2027/Conference†openreview.net . Please keep in mind that the deadlines are final and we cannot make any accommodations for missing the abstract deadline or paper deadline.
L95: # Submission instructions
L96: ## Deadlines
L97: Authors must submit paper abstracts by the abstract submission deadline of Sep 18, 2026 AOE. Please note that no authors can be added or removed after the abstract submission deadline (author order can be changed after the abstract submission deadline up to the full paper deadline). Also, please make sure that all authors have an OpenReview profile with the latest information.  Abstracts submitted by the abstract submission deadline must be genuine; placeholder or duplicate abstracts will be removed.
L98: The full paper submission deadline is Sep 25, 2026 AOE. Abstracts and papers must be submitted using the conference submission system at: cite28†https://openreview.net/group?id=ICLR.cc/2027/Conference†openreview.net .
L99: ## Author order
L100: It is key that authors submit genuine and informative abstracts that reflect the content of the full submission, as abstracts will be used in reviewer bidding before the final paper submission deadline. Placeholder or duplicate abstracts will be removed. However, titles and abstracts may be edited before the submission deadline. Author order may be edited after the abstract deadline, but new authors cannot be added or removed. No changes to authors are permitted after the submission deadline.
L101: No changes to title are permitted after the submission deadline until the end of the discussion period.
L102: ## Double-blind submission and anonymity
L103: 
L104: ICLR 2027 is double blind, which means that all submitted papers should be anonymous. Any paper where author identity is revealed in either the main text or the supplementary material will be desk rejected. Note that related arxiv papers by the same authors do not break anonymity; if cited, these should be cited in third person.
L105: ## Paper formatting
L106: 
L107: At the time of submission, the main text should be 9 pages or fewer. During the discussion/rebuttal phase and for the camera ready, the page limit will be increased to 10 pages to allow for new results/discussions. This limit will be strictly enforced. Papers with main text beyond the page limit will be desk-rejected.
L108: 
L109: The list of references does not count towards the page limit, and unlimited additional pages are allowed for the bibliography/references.
L110: Authors may use as many pages of appendices (after the bibliography) as they wish, but reviewers are not required to read the appendix.
L111: 
L112: Style files and Templates: To prepare your submission to ICLR 2027, please use the LaTeX style files provided at: cite29†https://media.iclr.cc/Conferences/ICLR2027/iclr-2027-style-files.zip†media.iclr.cc L113: ## Supplementary Materials
L114: 
L115: Supplementary (text) submission: We encourage authors to submit a single file (paper + supplementary text). Supplementary text should appear after the references. Please mark the supplementary material clearly (e.g. as an appendix).
L116: Supplementary code and other supplementary materials: Source code associated with a paper can be uploaded as part of the supplementary material. Code submission gives more information to reviewers, especially for replicability of the paper. We encourage all authors to submit code as part of their submission. Note that reviewers are encouraged, but not required to review supplementary material during the review process.
L117: ## Required: AI use statement
L118: 
L119: (See the cite26†AI Policy for Authors for more details.) This section does not count toward the page limit.
L120: ## Recommended: Ethics statement
L121: 
L122: All ICLR participants, including authors, are required to adhere to the ICLR Code of Ethics ( cite30†https://iclr.cc/public/CodeOfEthics ). All authors of submitted papers are required to read the Code of Ethics, adhere to it, and explicitly acknowledge this during the submission process. The Code of Ethics applies to all conference participation, including paper submission, reviewing, and paper discussion.
L123: As part of the review process, reviewers will be encouraged to raise potential violations of the ICLR Code of Ethics. If authors feel that their paper submission raises questions regarding the Code of Ethics, they are encouraged to include a paragraph of Ethics Statement (at the end of the main text before references) to address potential concerns where appropriate.
L124: Topics include, but are not limited to, studies that involve human subjects, practices to data set releases, potentially harmful insights, methodologies and applications, potential conflicts of interest and sponsorship, discrimination/bias/fairness concerns, privacy and security issues, legal compliance, and research integrity issues (e.g., IRB, documentation, research ethics). The optional ethics statement will not count toward the page limit, but should not be more than 1 page.
L125: ## Recommended: Reproducibility statement
L126: It is important that the work published in ICLR is reproducible. Authors are strongly encouraged to include a paragraph-long Reproducibility Statement at the end of the main text (before references) to discuss the efforts that have been made to ensure reproducibility. This paragraph should not itself describe details needed for reproducing the results, but rather reference the parts of the main paper, appendix, and supplemental materials that will help with reproducibility.
L127: For example, for novel models or algorithms, a link to an anonymous downloadable source code can be submitted as supplementary materials; for theoretical results, clear explanations of any assumptions and a complete proof of the claims can be included in the appendix; for any datasets used in the experiments, a complete description of the data processing steps can be provided in the supplementary materials. Each of the above are examples of things that can be referenced in the reproducibility statement.
L128: This optional reproducibility statement is not part of the main text and therefore will not count toward the page limit.
L129: # Policies
L130: 
L131: ## Author Identity
L132: 
L133: All ICLR submitters must have an OpenReview profile. If you do not have a profile already, create one as soon as possible. New profiles created without an institutional email will go through a moderation process that can take up to two weeks. New profiles created with an institutional email will be activated automatically.
L134: 
L135: Authors are responsible for ensuring that their profiles are up to date to facilitate reciprocal reviewing requirements.
L136: ## Quotas
L137: 
L138: No author may appear as a co-author on more than 20 papers.
L139: Each author may appear as a co-author on at most one paper in which no author is an eligible reciprocal reviewer. In plain language: if you, and all of your co-authors, have never had a paper accepted for publication in a major machine learning conference or journal, you may submit at most one paper to ICLR this year. See “Reciprocal reviewing requirement” below for the list of eligible conferences and journals.
L140: As noted there, eligibility is determined based on accepted papers as of the abstract deadline.
L141: Submissions in excess of either quota will be flagged during the abstract submission period. If they are still exceeded at the time of full paper submissions, we will randomly desk-reject excess submissions until every author is under quota.
L142: 
L143: [Why these new policies? The rapid rate of growth in submissions, while exciting, has begun to strain the review system, and we believe these limits are necessary to provide a fair and informative review process to all submitters.]
L144: ## Reciprocal Reviewing Requirement
L145: 
L146: Following previous conferences, there is a requirement for authors to serve as reviewers based on the number of papers they submit.
L147: All authors who are on 3 or more papers must serve as a reviewer for at least 6 papers. Authors in this category that fail to produce complete, high-quality reviews by the rebuttal stage may have their paper submissions desk rejected. Authors are exempt from the reviewing requirement if they are serving as an AC, SAC, or another organizing chair for ICLR 2027.
L148: In addition, all submissions must have at least one author who is registered to review at least 3 papers. The registered reviewer should be qualified to review, and they are qualified if they have at least one accepted publication at one of the following venues:
L149:   * ICLR / NeurIPS / ICML / UAI / AISTATS / JMLR / TMLR (includes "Datasets & Benchmarks")
L150:   * ACL / EMNLP / EACL / NAACL / IJCNLP-AACL / CL / TACL (includes "Findings")
L151:   * COLM
L152:   * CVPR / ICCV / ECCV / PAMI / 3DV (includes "Findings")
L153:   * AAAI / IJCAI / JAIR
L154:   * ICRA / IROS / RSS / CoRL
L155:   * KDD
L156:   * COLT
L157: Note that only primary conference papers satisfy the requirement; other publications associated with these conferences (including position papers, "tiny papers", blog posts, system demonstrations, industry papers, and workshop papers) do not satisfy the reciprocal reviewing requirement.
L158: Eligibiity is determined by papers accepted for publication by the abstract deadline. In particular, if your only qualifying publication is an accepted NeurIPS 2026 publication, you are not a qualified reciprocal reviewer.
L159: 
L160: (If you think something should be on this list but isn’t, please contact the PCs.)
L161: If none of the authors are qualified under this definition, then they are exempt from this requirement: we encourage submissions from researchers new to ICLR! However, as described above, such submissions are capped at one per author. Eligibility will be determined based on OpenReview profiles. Incorrect information on your profile will be grounds for desk rejection.
L162: All authors will be notified to register as reviewers after the abstract deadline. If none of the authors are registered as a reviewer, it will result in desk rejection for the paper. The program chairs may grant exceptions on a case-by-case basis.
L163: ## Dual Submission Policy
L164: Submissions that are identical (or substantially similar) to versions that have been previously published, or accepted for publication, or that have been submitted in parallel to this or other conferences or journals, are not allowed and violate our dual submission policy.
L165: However, papers that cite previous related work by the authors and papers that have appeared on non-peer reviewed websites (like arXiv) or that have been presented at workshops (i.e., venues that do not have publication proceedings) do not violate the policy. The policy is enforced during the whole reviewing process period. Submission of the paper to archival repositories such as arXiv is allowed during the review period.
L166: To allow citation of papers that are under review at ICLR2027, OpenReview provides BibTeX entries that do not list the authors, but does give the title, year and url. Author names are revealed at the end of the review period.

L170: ## Withdrawal Policy
L171: Authors have the right to withdraw papers from consideration at any time until an accept or reject decision has been announced. Before the paper submission deadline, if an author withdraws the paper it will be deleted from the OpenReview hosting site. However, note that after the paper submission deadline, if an author chooses to withdraw a submission, it will remain hosted by OpenReview in a publicly visible "withdrawn papers" section. Like on arXiv, submissions to ICLR cannot be deleted or modified.
L172: Withdrawn papers will be de-anonymized immediately. Papers submitted are considered archival for scientific purposes, and cannot be deleted.
L173: ## Code of Conduct
L174: 
L175: All ICLR participants, including authors, are required to adhere to the ICLR code of conduct (cite31†https://iclr.cc/public/CodeOfConduct ). More detailed guidance for authors, reviewers, and all other participants will be made available in due course, and participation will require acknowledging and adhering to the provided guidelines.
L176: ## Code of Ethics
L177: 
L178: All ICLR participants, including authors, are required to adhere to the ICLR Code of Ethics (https://iclr.cc/public/CodeOfEthics). All authors of submitted papers are required to read the Code of Ethics, adhere to it, and explicitly acknowledge this during the submission process. The Code of Ethics applies to all conference participation, including paper submission, reviewing, and paper discussion.
L179: ## Sanctioned Entities and Institutions
L180: 
L181: Because ICLR is incorporated in the US, we are not permitted to accept submissions from entities and individuals that are subject to US sanctions. A complete list may be found here https://sanctionslist.ofac.treas.gov/Home/SdnList. Submissions discovered to be affiliated with entities on this list will be desk-rejected.
L182: # Reviewing Process
L183: 
L184: Double blind reviewing: Submissions will be double blind: reviewers cannot see author names when conducting reviews, and authors cannot see reviewer names. Having papers on arxiv is allowed per the dual submission policy outlined above.
